items.title: 수입 찾는 20대는 이거 읽어두면 첫 달 안 날림
items.summary:
수입 찾는 20대는 이거 읽어두면 첫 달 안 날림
월 40만원 벌던 25살이 월매출 1억 찍은 아마존 구매대행 5단계

군 전역 후 적금 300만원으로 시작한 대표가 직접 공개한 월매출 1억대 아마존 구매대행 운영 화면과 5단계 공정

아마존 구매대행은 10년 된 레드오션이라 마진이 안 남고, 중국 도매만 뒤지면 된다는 말을 그대로 믿으면 안 된다는 걸 알게 됨. 이분은 남들과 같은 방식이 아니라 마진 30% 이상 나오는 상품만 고르는 게 핵심이라고 말함

이분은 97년생 대표로, 군 적금 300만원으로 노트북 한 대를 사서 부모님 집에서 시작했다고 털어놓음. 처음 7개월은 하루 16~17시간씩 일하고도 순이익이 월 40만원이었다고 함. 그런데 지금은 하루 15~30분만 일한다며, 화면을 직접 새로고침해서 이번 달 매출 1억 2천만원을 보여줌. 가장 잘 나온 달은 매출 약 1억 8천만원, 마진은 30% 정도, 반품과 취소는 거의 0이라고 함 ㄷㄷ

이분이 제시한 구매대행 공정 5가지는 다음과 같음

1. 뭘 팔지 정하는 게 제일 어려움
초보가 가장 막히는 구간이 상품 고르기라고 짚음. 직접 만든 GPT 앱에 '오늘 핼러윈 상품 올릴 거야'라고 치면 아마존 베스트셀러 중 한국 취향에 맞는 걸 엑셀로 뽑아 줌. 그날 목록에는 고딕 장식, 유령 장식, 반려동물 의상이 올라옴. 재고가 없는 구조라 시즌 한 달 전이 아니라 내일부터 팔 수 있다는 점도 강조함.

2. 수집은 엑셀 넣고 버튼 하나
엑셀을 전용 프로그램에 넣으면 AI가 사진을 보고 카테고리를 알아서 맞춤. 시연 화면의 작업 기록에는 70시간 전에 돌린 수집이 21만 개를 모아 둔 상태였음. 예전엔 하루 3~10개 올렸는데 지금은 6만 개까지 올린다고 함.

3. 올리기 전에 팔리게 가공하기
번역된 상품명은 길고 어색해서, 'AI 상품 번역'을 누르면 한국 감각에 맞게 줄이고 네이버 글자 수 기준에도 맞춤. 상세페이지보다 클릭이 먼저라서 상품명과 태그로 노출 순위를 올리는 데 공을 들인다고 함.

4. 등록은 여섯 번 클릭
키보드를 치워 놓고 마우스로 여섯 번 눌러 스마트스토어와 쿠팡에 올리는 걸 보여줌. 찾기, 수집, 가공, 등록 네 단계가 이 안에서 끝남.

5. 주문은 아마존이 배송까지
주문이 들어오면 아마존 주소를 영어로 넣고 구매 버튼만 누르면 아마존이 배송을 하고 반품도 받아 줌. 고객 문의는 하루 3~4건 수준이고 이것도 AI가 맡는다고 함. 그래서 하루 15~30분이 가능하다는 설명임.

진짜 이런 거 보면 '자동화 프로그램'보다 '뭘 팔지 고르는 감각과 7개월 버틴 시간'이 필요한 이유가 있는듯. 매출 1억은 순이익이 아니라 마진 30% 기준으로 봐야 하고, 이 프로그램은 수강생 전용에 서버·개발비가 월 20만원이라 구독자에게는 1주일만 열어 준다고 했음. 영상 끝은 단톡방 가입 유도라 홍보 성격이 있고 수강생 성과도 개인별 사례일 뿐이라는 점은 걸러 봐야 함. 사업자 등록과 통관 같은 규정도 따로 확인해야 함

자동화는 맨 마지막에 오는 거구나 싶음

출처 : 유튜브 머니게이션 | 부업해서 1억 넘게 벌 수 있었던 이유?!?! 군대 전역 후 엄청난 수익을 낼 수 있었던 꿀팁!!

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Google AI policy forces decision for San Diego schools – NBC 7 San Diego
items.summary:
As districts consider their options, students are already seeing artificial intelligence become a more common part of everyday learning.

“I feel like I see a lot of people using AI now,” said Delilah Ortiz, a student at El Camino High School.

Some students believe the focus should be on establishing guidelines for AI use rather than banning the technology entirely. [...] San Diego County school districts face a January deadline to decide whether to opt in to Google's artificial intelligence features or lose access to the company's search engine, forcing educators to weigh the benefits of AI against concerns about student access to the technology. [...] Google plans to disable a range of AI-powered features, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search in January to give school districts more control over the technology students can access. However, districts that want to continue using Google Search will have to opt in to the AI features.

items.title: What is AI infrastructure? | Glossary | HPE
items.summary:
ML models: AI infrastructure relies on machine learning (ML) models, which recognize patterns and predict on massive datasets. To work efficiently, these models need lots of computing and storage power. They operate as the fundamental building blocks of artificial intelligence systems, powering various features from computer vision to natural language processing. [...] Generative AI: Generative AI applications use foundation models and large language models (LLMs) to create text, images, code, audio, and other content. These workloads require significant compute power, large datasets, and scalable storage resources to train, fine-tune, and deploy models effectively. [...] AI infrastructure provides the compute, storage, networking, software, and data resources required to support AI initiatives.
 Modern AI infrastructure is commonly used to support natural language processing, AI agents, predictive analytics, generative AI, and computer vision.
 High-performance hardware, scalable data platforms, and networking are critical components of AI infrastructure.

items.title: AI Should Have to Earn Its Future - Mozilla Foundation
items.summary:
For a few years now, we’ve asked whether AI is trustworthy. The better question is whether it’s worthy.

Trustworthy asks whether a system keeps its promise. Worthy asks whether that promise merits a teacher’s time, a city’s water, an artist’s work - and everything we might have built instead. Through that lens, AI might be an incredible unlock for certain human problems, and for others, the right amount of AI is none. [...] For a technology with planetary ambitions, this is a strangely provincial story. America keeps imagining the future of AI. Elsewhere, I found people imagining the future of human life, and asking whether AI had a useful role to play in it.

In recent months, from Beijing and Shanghai to the UN General Assembly and Doha, I’ve heard variations on that question. The conversations moved from the practical to the political to the spiritual. All began with human beings, not machines. [...] Different questions, same conviction: capability alone is not a mandate. The people get to decide what is worth building.

The mood gap is real. Ipsos found that AI products and services excite 83% of respondents in China, 63% in Mexico, and 33% in the United States. Enthusiasm isn’t agency; skepticism isn’t wisdom. Still, America’s cocktail of hype and dread is a local specialty and it travels badly.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: AI 一级市场开始打折了，而且是实打实地砍。
items.summary:
AI 一级市场开始打折了，而且是实打实地砍。

Anthropic 这周就启动 IPO 路演，赶在感恩节前挂牌。但估值预期已经从最高的 2 万亿美元，一路降到 1.2 到 1.3 万亿，有人甚至只肯给 1.1 万亿。上周科技股那波血洗，直接把潜在买家的心理价位压下来了。

OpenAI 这边同步缩水：估值从 1.5 万亿降到 1.25 万亿，融资规模从 300 亿砍到最多 200 亿，首笔 110 亿已经到账，软银、红杉这些老股东出的钱也都缩了。

我的态度是，这种时候别急着下结论。AI 到底是真需求还是阶段性亢奋，一级市场的估值正好处在最乱的时候，让各种消息再发酵一段时间，等价格自己把分歧跑出来。看不清的时候，不做判断也是一种判断。
